feedback:
Problem Description: Convert the bullet points to paragraph structure.

Tests: - T8 (blocker): In test.sh's write_suite, the synthesized JUnit failure message is literally "package failed to build without the solution patch". This exposes internal assessment terminology directly into output an agent would see. Use neutral wording, e.g. "package failed to build", and keep the compiler output as the failure body.
- T8: The build-failure fallback in test.sh is all-or-nothing: if any one of the four tested packages fails to build, every one of the 36 new tests is reported as failed, even for packages that compiled and whose tests actually passed. This degrades attribution and can mask a partially correct submission. Parse and preserve real outcomes for packages that produced them, and synthesize failures only for the packages that had no results because they failed to build.
- T4: Test_CDCColFilter_ConfigDriven does not exercise the production wiring it claims to mirror. It parses column_filter via cdc.NewConfig (correct) but then manually calls Store.EnableCDC with cdcCfg.ColumnFilter, rather than going through cmd/rqlited's createCDC. A solution that parses and applies column filters through direct APIs but never threads cdcCfg.ColumnFilter through createCDC would still pass. Route this test through createCDC or an equally direct server-start path.
- T4: Test_CDCColFilter_Store_LeadershipTransitionInvalidatesCache changes the schema before the leadership transfer, so SchemaVersion alone already detects the change on the new leader; the test does not isolate the leadership-triggered invalidation requirement. A solution that never invalidates on leadership acquisition, relying only on SchemaVersion, still passes. Construct a same-version stale-cache scenario at this level too (as the streamer-level unit test already does), not just a straightforward schema change.
- T4: No test exercises Hashicorp Raft's snapshot-restore path (FSM.Restore / Store.fsmRestore), which independently swaps the database file. Invalidation could be wired only into the normal Load path and this would go unnoticed.
- T4: No test exercises the chunked load command path (COMMAND_TYPE_LOAD_CHUNK in store/command_processor.go), a second, independent database-swap path alongside the standard load command.
- T4: No test exercises Store.ReadFrom (the boot/install-database path), a third independent database-swap path.
- T4: Test_CDCColFilter_Store_SchemaEvolution_RenameAfterWrite and the other same-transaction cases only use INSERT statements. Add a case that performs an UPDATE (carrying both old and new row images) alongside add/drop/rename DDL in the same transaction, asserting both row images against the final columns, since a solution could remap only the new row and miss the old one.
- T3: Several new test comments are long narrative explanations of hypothetical incorrect implementations (for example, walking through exactly what "a stale cache" or "an implementation that only inspected the first column" would do). This is considerably more verbose than the terse, largely comment-free style used elsewhere in these packages' existing tests. Trim these to short, factual comments consistent with the surrounding code.
